reviews.text: A painfully overrated film. Beyond the wonderful animation. This film leaves much to be desired. Its a not so subtle humiliation ritual for peter b parker. They make him a fat loser whos wife left him, hes poor, hes crying in the shower, he has nothing in life. Meanwhile the film tries to actively convince you miles is better in every way. He has few flaws to speak of beyond the tried and boring “the hero just doesnt know what theyre capable of yet” and only after he accepts himself hes able to be better than the other spider-men. Unsurprisingly theres miscegenation propaganda. Miles sexually harasses gwen stacy and rips her hair off. He idolizes his criminal uncle and disrespects his police father whos named after the confederate president. Who gives a fuck about miles im serious. Who the fuck actually likes this little jit. We’re supposed to believe hes a genius accepted into a prestigious school. But hes a fuckin idiot and he gets his universe’s peter killed by being retarded. Goddamn i hate this character. If you rank this movie higher than the raimi films you are a fuckin moron.

Look, we can animate! Don't pay attention to the consecutively disappointing, recycled tropes and plot holes though ^^ Looks pretty, right? Now the best thing is that you are going to eat it up because it is Spiderman!! And because it is Spiderman you don't even have to think for yourself because the plot is being spoon-fed to you, isn't that great? Look at our other movies that have the exact same character arc again and again all over!!! And we even have super hip music that you guys at your age enjoy! You're going to love it!! Rant : It seems that in general, people justify this audiovisual product by saying: "Oh, but it looks pretty!" I have a few problems with this. First of all, this kind of animation is also from the perspective of 2018 nowhere near revolutionary. It is not daring of them "to try a new style" since typical marvel fans are just eating everything up anyway. And it's marvel, they can afford it. This movie just wanted to be edgy but in the end produced the same recycled and overused marvel tropes as always. "It was my fault" before the random ass villain uncle dies, the shy new kid at school, main character suddenly gaining confidence and being able to do crazy things even though they couldn't do anything before.. Aunt May being in on the secret just for convenience's sake to keep the plot going? Also, how ironic that trying to force your movie to be self-aware about it's overused tropes just sheds more light on HOW OVERUSED YOUR TROPES ARE. It's like shooting yourself in the knee and laughing awkwardly while doing it. Half of the things that happened had no significance because, guess what? There was a magic USB-Stick that happened to have the perfect code to stop the big evil machine from blowing everything up, wow how convenient for the main character, he didn't even have to do anything... Oh, and the music felt insulting to my ears.

Parker and they say "𝘓𝘰𝘰𝘬𝘴 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘢 𝘤𝘩𝘪𝘭𝘥 𝘥𝘳𝘦𝘴𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘚𝘱𝘪𝘥𝘦𝘳-𝘔𝘢𝘯 𝘥𝘳𝘢𝘨𝘨𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘢 𝘩𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘭𝘦𝘴𝘴 𝘤𝘰𝘳𝘱𝘴𝘦 𝘣𝘦𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘥 𝘢 𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘪𝘯." I felt that this didn't expand upon 𝘢𝘯𝘺 of the characters well enough, which is SO sad considering the sheer number of them, I mean we hardly even get to know Miles and that SUCKS!!!! From the bottom of my heart, I hope we get another movie that actually wholly delves into Miles Morales story. I want Spider-Man movies to go much further into 𝘸𝘩𝘰 𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘺 𝘢𝘳𝘦 as people, their motivations, hopes, etc. This felt lacklustre, which perhaps is due to the short run-time? They tried to cram too much shit into an hour and 56 minute movie- and it suffered for it. Not even to mention the villains were incredibly shallowly characterized, especially Olivia Octavius, of whom we know next to nothing about; she has zero personality, no interesting traits...and her design is awful! Those dreadful plastic-y tentacles of hers are reminiscent of children's toys. Ugh! Then there's how idiotic everything is about Kingpin, I couldn't stand anytime he was on screen due to his dreadful design- sorry, why does he look like a fucking wall in sheer mass, as well as resembling an egg? Is he supposed to be Kingpin or Humpty Dumpty.......... The soundtrack is excruciating...I had to mute multiple times just to finish this, why the hell would you subject me to Post Malone! That's plain torture. And I get that's dramatic to say but it's /really/ fucking bad, and I'm used to hating the song choices in film, like ?? try harder. Another thing is that, while I understand they were going for a "comic book aesthetic" sort of thing with the designs and art choices in general as...y'know, Spider-Man is a comic character, they just failed to do it effectively. For something so praised I expected much better art direction and designs.

You already know the story, so I ain’t gonna resume it So, I am not the biggest Spider-Man fan, not even what you would call a “fan”, but the movie was, alright, like, yes, I didn’t dislike it, but it’s not all “ WOW! ABSOLUTE CINEMA! ” For me, like yes! I'll watch Across The Spider-Verse, but I don’t really expect it to be a 5 star film for me, since your rating for any Spider-Man film depends a bit on how much of a “fan” you are in my opinion, the story's nice, some predictable things, the animation is great but not only because the animation is great means I will love a film, it always depends on how I see the story, plot, acting, etc, and my own enjoyment, though overrated, my rant is because I am pretty sure like 90% of 5 star reviews are just Spider-Man fans, which, it isn’t wrong to be a fan, but not because it’s a piece of media from a franchise means it’s necessarily 5 stars, everyone talking about the animation when, yes it’s nice and has good animators and shit BUT DOES THAT MAKE THE WHOLE FILM GOOD?!….for me? No. What matters is the story and plot for me, unless your animation is choppy and just shitty and that’s when it matters, if you’re a huge animation studio good animation is expected, I just don’t really connect with Spider-Man, sorry but, as much as I try to enjoy the films maximum I have ever given to a Spider-Man film (so far) is 4/5 stars, like I get why people are fans but, I just…it isn’t my thing! I can watch the films but it wouldn’t be my first choice! No, since I am autistic that doesn’t mean I have to love Spider-Man, each person will have their own opinion and thoughts, that’s basically all for my review/rant.

There were some cool moments but this is no where near the other Spider-Man movies for me let alone touching a top 20 marvel movie.

Looks pretty but a narrative mess. You can clearly see the seams where different narratives get welded together, too bad all lead to nowhere. Too many villains, and only Kingpin gets a motive that is PeterB's counterpart, neither of which get explored, we only see the resolution. Instead we get a coming-of-age story with Miles Morales, a teen that has it all, but having contempt for it; it just don't sit right with him. His new private school is too elitist, but we only see him having trouble socially as well as being overwhelmed with schoolwork, good thing  he's an A+ student. Why does he want to become Spiderman? No idea, sure he saw his masked weirdo get killed in front of him, but others came, other that were far more capable that were not keen on having dead weight to lug around. The idea of not doing schoolwork was part of his plan, but bailing on being Spiderman wasn't. Is that his motivation, looking cool? Why was he so eager to get the Spider-people's approval? Miles' story is that of an uncomplicated character: he gets everything, does the right thing and the only blemish is his character is the fact that he idolised a crook. Funny thing is it gets resolved immediately. Don't you worry, your favourite Miles Sue is super dooper simple to understand: he is perfect, yuppie!

I will never enjoy any installment in this franchise because the original Art Director, who is responsible for everything people loved about the animation, was fired after 2 years of working on the movie, and credited solely as a “Visual Consultant” despite so many of his initial storyboards and animation tests being copied clip for clip included in the final cut. Alberto Mielgo, the guy who made The Witness and Jibaro on Love, Death, and Robots, wanted to revolutionize animation and change the industry. He did that, but was robbed of all the credit. We genuinely could’ve had something so much more incredible if Sony wasn’t so afraid of taking chances. Anyway go open this link: Alberto Mielgo’s original concept art for Spider-Verse
